# Beeps

> Generates a coherent set of eleven interface sounds — tap, toggle on and off,
> open, close, send, receive, success, error, notification, delete —
> synthesized in the browser with Web Audio rather than sampled. No audio files
> to host, nothing to license, and a handoff written for a coding agent.

Free, no account, no API key, no rate limit. Every sound set is a pure function
of the URL, so the same link always returns the same sounds.

## Why this exists

Color has ramps and tokens. Motion has curves and durations. Sound has a folder
of MP3s someone found, at inconsistent levels, in no relationship to each other.
An agent asked to "add a success sound" has nothing to reach for. This produces
a set where every sound is derived from one base frequency, paired sounds are
exact inversions of each other, and loudness is normalized across the set.

## Using this as a tool

Build a URL and fetch it. **You do not need to run JavaScript** — the server
injects the whole set into the HTML as both a `<pre>` block and a
`<script type="application/json">`, so a plain fetch of any URL below returns
readable data. (Both shapes on purpose: HTML-to-markdown conversion strips
script tags, so JSON alone would be invisible to the tools most likely to be
reading this.)

If you want data without the page around it, `/api/sounds` takes the same
query string:

- `https://www.beeps.studio/api/sounds` — the default set, as JSON
- `https://www.beeps.studio/api/sounds?format=text` — the same, as plain text
- `https://www.beeps.studio/api/sounds?p=crisp` — a different character

It returns every sound with its tier, length, frequency range and its play/do-not-play
rules, plus the tier budgets and the preset list. One thing it deliberately omits:
`normalizedGain`. Loudness normalization is measured from a real render, which
needs Web Audio, so the browser computes it and this endpoint cannot. Sounds
played from the page are level-matched; these parameters alone are not.

The page itself takes the same parameters:

- `https://www.beeps.studio/` — the default set
- `https://www.beeps.studio/?p=crisp` — a different character
- `https://www.beeps.studio/?p=warm&tap=vcrisp.a2` — one sound in another voice, with an edit

### Set-level parameters

| Param | Required | Values | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `p` | no | `soft` (default), `minimal`, `crisp`, `warm`, `bloopy`, `glassy`, `playful`, `retro`, `scifi` | The character preset. Applies to the whole set. |
| `b` | no | 220–2000 | Base frequency in Hz. Every sound is an interval from this, so moving it transposes the set and keeps it in tune. Omit to use the preset's own. |

### Per-sound parameters

One parameter per sound, named after it. `toggle.on` and `toggle.off` are
written `toggle-on` and `toggle-off`, because a dot is the field separator.

The value is dot-separated fields, each a letter followed by a number:
`tap=f720.d100.g-3`. Omit any field to keep what the preset derives — only
what you change needs to appear.

| Field | Unit | Range | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `f` | Hz | 20–20000 | Start frequency of the primary voice. |
| `e` | Hz | 20–20000 | End frequency. Above `f` the sound rises; below, it falls. |
| `a` | ms | 0.5–200 | Attack. Single digits are what separate a click from a beep. |
| `d` | ms | 1–1000 | Decay. |
| `r` | ms | 1–1000 | Release. |
| `w` | ms | 1–2000 | How long the pitch takes to travel from `f` to `e`. |
| `g` | dB | −40–12 | Level trim against the sound's tier. Negative is quieter. |
| `c` | Hz | 80–20000 | Filter cutoff. |
| `q` | ×10 | 0–200 | Filter resonance, times ten — `q7` is a Q of 0.7. |
| `v` | — | any preset id | That sound's voice: which preset it is played on. Pitch stays global. |

Anything out of range is clamped rather than rejected, and an unparseable field
is dropped with a note on the page. A link always resolves to a playable set.

## The set

| Sound | Tier | Plays when | Does not play when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tap` | subtle | A discrete press that commits something small — a button, a segment, a menu item. | Hover, focus, scroll, or any pointer movement. Never on every keystroke. |
| `toggle.on` | subtle | A binary control turning on, when the user turned it on. | Programmatic state changes, or restoring saved settings on load. |
| `toggle.off` | subtle | The same control turning off. | Programmatic state changes, or restoring saved settings on load. |
| `open` | subtle | A surface the user opened: menu, sheet, drawer, disclosure. | Anything that opens by itself, including tooltips on hover. |
| `close` | subtle | The same surface dismissed. | Route changes and page navigation — those are not closes. |
| `send` | notable | Outbound, user-initiated: a message sent, a form submitted, a job queued. | Autosave, background sync, telemetry, retries. |
| `receive` | notable | Inbound content arriving while the user is present and looking. | Bulk arrivals — play once for a batch, never once per item. |
| `success` | notable | A user-initiated operation completed, and only one they were waiting for. | Background success, cache warms, or anything they did not start. Never as a page-load chime. |
| `error` | alert | An operation failed in a way the user must respond to. | Validation on a field they have not finished typing in. Never more than once per submit. |
| `notification` | alert | An interruption that is genuinely new information. | Anything the user can see happening. Never when the tab is focused and the item is already on screen. |
| `delete` | notable | Destructive removal that has actually happened. | Opening a confirmation dialog — that is `open`. |

Tiers set how much attention a sound asks for, and drive both its level and its
length: `subtle` runs 70–180 ms, `notable` 90–450, `alert` 120–700.

## Rules the set is built on

These are worth knowing if you are going to edit the numbers.

- **One base frequency.** Every sound is an interval from it, so the set stays
  in tune when you move it. Editing one sound does not detune the others.
- **Pairs invert by construction.** `open`/`close`, `send`/`receive` and
  `toggle.on`/`toggle.off` traverse the same two notes in opposite directions.
  Editing one moves the other; they cannot be set to disagree.
- **Every sound lands on a consonant interval** — unison, major second, major
  third, fourth, fifth or major sixth. A falling sound landing between two
  notes reads as sad and slightly broken rather than as neutral.
- **Direction carries meaning.** A preset may flatten a pitch move but never
  reverse one.
- **Loudness is normalized** across the set by A-weighted RMS, measured per
  sound at render time, so nothing jumps out. Not LUFS: BS.1770 gates on 400 ms
  blocks and every sound here is shorter than one block.
- **There is a duration floor, not just a ceiling.** The ear integrates loudness
  over roughly 100–200 ms, so a burst under about 70 ms is heard as *quieter*
  rather than subtler — up to 10–15 dB down — and you get nothing back for the
  room you saved.

## Exports

Everything is generated client-side; there is no build step and no CDN.

- **WAV** — 44.1 kHz, 16-bit, mono.
- **Data URI** — the same WAV inline, for dropping straight into a stylesheet
  or a script with no file to serve.
- **JavaScript** — a zero-dependency synthesis function. Ships the sounds as
  parameters, not audio, so it costs a few hundred bytes rather than a few
  hundred kilobytes. Muted until you enable it.
- **JSON** — every sound with every frequency, envelope and filter resolved.
- **Markdown** — the table above plus the parameters, written to be pasted into
  an agent's context.

## Rules for using these sounds

If you are wiring these into a product, the `whenNot` column matters more than
the `when` column. The common failure is not a bad sound, it is a good sound
played too often.

- Nothing should autoplay. Sound stays off until a user asks for it, and the
  exported runtime defaults to muted.
- One sound per user action. Not one per state change, and never one per item
  in a batch.
- Do not sound anything the user can already see happening.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` as a hint that a quieter interface is wanted.

## Other tools in this family

Same contract everywhere: state lives in the query string, every page serves its
values as plain text without JavaScript, and there is no account, key or rate
limit. Generated from the shared manifest — see `src/shared/tools.ts`.
